what_it_does: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) are a style of AI model inspired by biological neurons: instead of passing continuous numbers between layers, neurons fire discrete binary "spikes" (a 1 or a 0). Because most spikes are zero, prior hardware designs save energy by simply skipping the multiplications where the spike is zero. This paper observes a further opportunity: if two different neurons happen to have spikes at exactly the same set of positions in the same timestep, then the weighted sum (dot product) they would each compute with the next layer's weights will be identical, so you only need to compute it once and share the result. The Prosperity accelerator implements this idea by hashing each neuron's spike pattern into a compact fingerprint in real time, grouping neurons with matching fingerprints, computing the shared dot product once, and broadcasting the result to every neuron in the group. This works for both the fully-connected and convolutional (spatially-sliding) parts of an SNN.
